title: Operator-signature mismatch causing int4 hotpath crashloops and capacity churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A recent quantizer/converter change introduced subtle operator-signature rewrites for fused attention kernels on int4 paths. The converter emitted an unsupported op pattern for certain dynamic-shape transformer layers which the runtime kernel selector could not match; the fallback logic attempted to route requests to an incompatible kernel variant, triggering repeated SIGSEGVs in the int4 hotpath. Affected Dedicated pools and a subset of hosted nodes entered CrashLoopBackOff / unhealthy state, triggering autoscaler churn and temporary capacity shortfall for high-throughput tenants. This ticket tracks the incident follow-ups, immediate mitigations, and long-term safeguards.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC - Deploy: quant-converter v2.9 rolled into canary cluster via runtime-1.21
2026-03-09 02:45 UTC - First errors: automated chaos detector flagged increased OOM/crash-restarter rate on canary int4 hosts
2026-03-09 03:10 UTC - Pager: oncall notified after 5% of dedicated pools report >=3 restarts in 10m
2026-03-09 03:35 UTC - Investigation: core dumps showed illegal instruction in third-party fused-kernel shim called from int4 dispatcher
2026-03-09 04:02 UTC - Rollback: canary unrolled to quant-converter v2.8; crashes subsided on canary but two Dedicated node groups still had unhealthy instances
2026-03-09 06:20 UTC - Mitigation: mark affected kernel variant as disabled in runtime hotpatch; autoscaler settings adjusted to avoid aggressive draining until further analysis
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Post-incident triage meeting; RCA assigned to quant infra and runtime teams
root_cause_summary: The quant-converter change introduced an operator signature rewrite that transformed a supported op-sequence into a fused op pattern with a slightly different attribute ordering. The runtime kernel matcher uses a fingerprint that is sensitive to attribute order and shape qualifiers; the new pattern failed to match any compatible kernel. Fallback logic attempted to select an alternative kernel but passed mismatched metadata (shape aliasing) which led to memory-safety violations in the int4 fused shim. Combined with aggressive Dedicated autoscaler drain policies, this produced capacity churn and customer-facing throttling for high-throughput tenants.
impact_details: Duration: ~2h of elevated error rates and rolling restarts on affected Dedicated pools during 2026-03-09 UTC maintenance window
Customers: 3 enterprise tenants experienced elevated 5xx rates and increased latency; one customer observed traffic rationing due to autoscaler capacity contraction
Operational: Autoscaler performed multiple node replacements resulting in increased GPU-hours and billing exposure; oncall load increased and escalation to SRE was required
immediate_mitigations: Hotpatch: disabled the offending fused kernel variant via runtime feature flag (runtime hotpatch id: HP-2026-03-09-17)
Rollback: reverted quant-converter to v2.8 in affected clusters and blocked v2.9 rollout until testing added
Autoscaler config: temporarily relaxed drain_ratio and increased stabilization window to prevent cascade churn
Customer comms: Sent targeted incident notices to affected customers with remediation steps and ETA for full fix

postmortem_notes: Lessons learned: our kernel matching logic assumed a stable attribute ordering contract between converter and runtime; converter maintenance can change ordering when refactors occur. Operator contracts must be explicit and tested end-to-end.
Preventative measures: implement compatibility tests, add tolerant fingerprinting, and require a 24h bounded synthetic canary for any converter/change touching fused ops or int4 paths.
Longer term: consider formalizing an 'operator ABI' with versioning and guarded feature flags to avoid silent mismatches across components.
